question: did the two judges agree on the no-span items because they judged, or because retrieval failed for both
design: the nine items where cue retrieval returned no candidate span were re-judged by both models on the full artifact instead of on retrieved spans
finding: four of nine items that the pipeline scored as not satisfied without any model call are judged satisfied by both models when the full artifact is shown. The agreement on those items was an artefact of a shared retrieval failure, not a judgement.

consequence_for_the_endpoint.assumption_falsified: RD-2026-09-02-14A demoted cue matching to a high-recall candidate filter and built the endpoint on filter plus verification. That design assumed the filter rarely misses. On these items it misses at least four of nine.
consequence_for_the_endpoint.effect: the verified endpoint understates coverage whenever the filter misses, and the miss is silent because no model is ever called
consequence_for_the_endpoint.not_yet_quantified: this measures only the items where retrieval returned nothing. Items where retrieval returned a poor span are not covered and could fail in the same direction

why_the_earlier_agreement_figures_are_un: the cross-judge replication excluded the no-span items from its denominator, so the reported 0.667 and the band figures do not include them
immediate_effect: the high-recall assumption is recorded as falsified; the endpoint needs a retrieval step whose recall is measured rather than assumed
